text: Annual Leave Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Entitlement All full-time employees accrue 20 days of paid annual leave per calendar year (pro-rated for part-time employees based on contracted hours). Accrual begins on the first day of employment. Employees in their first year accrue leave monthly at a rate of 1.67 days per month. Requesting Leave Leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least five business days in advance for absences of one to three days, and at least fifteen business days in advance for absences of four or more consecutive days. Requests are subject to manager approval and must consider team coverage requirements. Managers should respond within three business days of a request being submitted. Carry-Over Up to 5 days of unused annual leave may be carried over into the following calendar year. Carried-over leave must be used before March 31 or it will lapse. No cash payment is made for lapsed leave. Leave on Termination Upon termination of employment, accrued and unused annual leave will be paid out at the employee's current base daily rate. Public Holidays Public holidays are in addition to annual leave entitlement. Where an employee is required to work on a public holiday, they will receive a day off in lieu to be taken within 60 days.

Sick Leave Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Entitlement Full-time employees are entitled to 10 days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Sick leave does not accrue — the full balance is available from January 1 each year (or from the date of hire for new joiners). Unused sick leave does not carry over and is not paid out on termination. Notification Employees must notify their manager by 9:00 AM on the first day of absence, or as early as reasonably practicable. Notification should be made by phone or messaging platform, not email alone. Medical Certification For absences of three or more consecutive days, a medical certificate from a registered practitioner must be provided within two business days of returning to work. The company reserves the right to request a certificate for any absence where a pattern of short-term absences has been observed. Extended Illness If an employee exhausts their paid sick leave entitlement, additional absence may be covered by: 1. Annual leave (at the employee's request) 2. Unpaid medical leave, approved by People Operations Employees on extended medical leave of more than four consecutive weeks should contact People Operations to discuss return-to-work planning and any available accommodations.

Return to Work Following an absence of five or more consecutive days, employees are required to complete a return-to-work discussion with their manager before resuming full duties.

Remote Work Policy Effective date: March 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Eligibility Remote work arrangements are available to employees whose roles do not require a consistent physical presence (e.g., on-site lab work, hardware maintenance, front-desk roles). Eligibility is determined by the employee's manager in consultation with People Operations. Hybrid Schedule The default arrangement is hybrid: employees are expected to be in the office a minimum of two days per week. Specific anchor days (days when whole teams are expected in-person) are set by department heads and communicated at least two weeks in advance. Fully Remote Arrangements Fully remote arrangements require written approval from the employee's department head and People Operations. Requests should be submitted using the Remote Work Request Form and will be reviewed within ten business days. Equipment and Workspace The company provides a standard laptop and peripherals. Employees are responsible for maintaining a safe, distraction-free workspace and a reliable internet connection (minimum 25 Mbps download / 10 Mbps upload recommended). A one-time home office stipend of $500 is available to employees on approved fully remote arrangements. Claims must be submitted within 90 days of approval. Security Remote employees must: - Connect to company systems via the approved VPN. - Not work from public Wi-Fi without VPN active. - Lock their screen whenever stepping away. - Store all company data in approved cloud storage, not on local drives.

Availability Remote employees are expected to be reachable during core hours (10:00 AM – 4:00 PM in their local time zone) and to attend all scheduled meetings with camera on unless technical issues prevent it. Review Remote work arrangements are reviewed annually or whenever the employee's role or performance status changes significantly.

Expense Reimbursement Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: Finance & People Operations Scope This policy applies to all employees incurring business expenses on behalf of the company. Personal expenses are not reimbursable under any circumstances. Submission Deadlines Expense reports must be submitted within 30 days of the expense being incurred. Reports submitted after 60 days will not be reimbursed without written approval from the CFO. Pre-Approval Requirements The following require written pre-approval from the employee's manager before the expense is incurred: - Any single expense over $500 - International travel - Conference registrations over $300 - Software or subscription purchases Travel Flights: Economy class for all flights under 6 hours. Business class is permitted for flights of 6 hours or more, subject to manager approval. Hotels: Up to $250/night in standard cities; up to $350/night in high-cost cities (New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich, Tokyo). Exceptions require VP-level approval. Ground transport: Rideshare or taxi is reimbursable when public transit is impractical. Personal car use is reimbursed at the current IRS standard mileage rate. Meals while travelling: Up to $75/day, excluding alcohol. Alcohol is never reimbursable. Meals and Entertainment Business meals with clients or prospects are reimbursable up to $100/person. The expense report must include the names and company affiliations of all attendees and the business purpose.

The expense report must include the names and company affiliations of all attendees and the business purpose. Internal team meals are reimbursable up to $40/person and require manager approval. Receipts Original itemised receipts are required for all expenses over $25. Credit card statements are not acceptable as sole documentation. Reimbursement Timeline Approved expense reports are processed within 10 business days and paid via the employee's regular payroll or direct bank transfer. Non-Reimbursable Items - Alcohol (in any context) - Personal entertainment, mini-bar charges, in-flight Wi-Fi for personal use - Traffic or parking fines - Expenses for family members or guests not on company business - Clothing or personal grooming

Employee Onboarding Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Purpose This policy ensures every new employee has a consistent, structured start that gives them the context, tools, and relationships they need to contribute effectively. Pre-boarding (Before Day 1) People Operations is responsible for: - Sending a welcome email with first-day logistics at least three business days before start date. - Provisioning accounts (email, HR portal, Slack, code repositories) so they are ready on day one. - Shipping or arranging collection of equipment at least two business days before start date. - Assigning an onboarding buddy from the same or an adjacent team. The hiring manager is responsible for: - Preparing a 30/60/90-day plan and sharing it with the new hire in the welcome email. - Scheduling intro meetings with key stakeholders in the first two weeks. Week 1 Day Activity ----- ----------- Day 1 IT setup, HR portal orientation, team introductions, office tour Day 2 Benefits enrollment (must be completed within 5 business days) Day 3 Compliance training: Code of Conduct, Data Privacy, Security Awareness Day 4–5 Role-specific tool setup and initial project briefing 30/60/90-Day Milestones 30 days: New hire has completed all mandatory compliance training, understands team processes, and has made a first meaningful contribution.

Compliance training: Code of Conduct, Data Privacy, Security Awareness Day 4–5 Role-specific tool setup and initial project briefing 30/60/90-Day Milestones 30 days: New hire has completed all mandatory compliance training, understands team processes, and has made a first meaningful contribution. 60 days: New hire is operating independently on assigned tasks and has completed a first check-in with their manager using the onboarding check-in template. 90 days: Formal onboarding closes. Manager and new hire complete the 90-day review form in the HR portal. Any unresolved gaps are documented with an action plan. Onboarding Buddy Each new hire is paired with an onboarding buddy for their first 60 days. The buddy's role is informal: answer day-to-day questions, make social introductions, and help the new hire navigate company norms. Buddies are not responsible for performance management. Mandatory Training The following must be completed within the first 10 business days: - Code of Conduct - Data Privacy and GDPR Awareness - Information Security Basics - Anti-Harassment and Inclusion Completion is tracked automatically in the Learning Management System. Failure to complete within the deadline will be escalated to the new hire's manager.

Performance Review Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Review Cycle Performance reviews are conducted twice per year: - Mid-year review: Completed in July. Primarily a development-focused check-in; no compensation changes result directly from this cycle. - Annual review: Completed in December. Informs compensation adjustments, promotion decisions, and the following year's goal-setting. New employees hired within three months of a review cycle are exempt from that cycle and will participate in the next one. Process 1. Goal-setting: At the start of each year (or within 30 days of hire), employees set 3–5 SMART goals in the HR portal in collaboration with their manager. 2. Self-assessment: Employees complete a self-assessment form in the HR portal at least five business days before their scheduled review meeting. 3. Manager assessment: Managers complete their assessment independently before the review meeting. 4. Review meeting: A 60-minute 1:1 between employee and manager to discuss performance, development areas, and goals. 5. Calibration: Managers participate in a calibration session with their peer group to ensure rating consistency before results are finalised. 6. Outcome communication: Final ratings and any compensation changes are communicated to employees within two weeks of calibration closing. Rating Scale Rating Description -------- ------------- 5 – Exceptional Consistently exceeds all goals; significant impact beyond role scope 4 – Exceeds expectations Meets all goals and exceeds several; demonstrably above role level 3 – Meets expectations Meets all or most goals; fully effective in role 2 – Partially meets expectations Meets some goals; improvement needed in key areas 1 – Does not meet expectations Significant gaps; performance improvement plan required

role level 3 – Meets expectations Meets all or most goals; fully effective in role 2 – Partially meets expectations Meets some goals; improvement needed in key areas 1 – Does not meet expectations Significant gaps; performance improvement plan required Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs) Employees receiving a rating of 1 will be placed on a formal PIP within 10 business days of the review. A PIP document specifies measurable improvement targets, a timeline (typically 60–90 days), and the support the employee will receive. People Operations must be involved in all PIPs. Appeals Employees may appeal their rating by submitting a written request to People Operations within 10 business days of receiving their review outcome. Appeals are reviewed by the employee's skip-level manager and a People Operations representative.

Code of Conduct Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: Legal & People Operations Our Commitment We are committed to maintaining a workplace where every person is treated with dignity and respect. This Code of Conduct applies to all employees, contractors, and anyone acting on the company's behalf — in the office, while travelling on business, at company events, and in online interactions related to work. Expected Behaviours - Integrity: Be honest in all professional dealings. Do not misrepresent your work, qualifications, or the company. - Respect: Treat colleagues, customers, and partners with courtesy regardless of role, background, or opinion. - Collaboration: Share information openly, give credit generously, and resolve disagreements constructively. - Accountability: Take ownership of your work and its outcomes. Raise problems early; don't hide mistakes. - Confidentiality: Protect proprietary information, customer data, and colleague details as outlined in the Data Privacy Policy. Prohibited Conduct The following behaviours are grounds for disciplinary action up to and including termination: - Harassment, bullying, or intimidation of any kind (see Anti-Harassment Policy) - Discrimination based on race, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic - Dishonesty, fraud, or falsification of records - Misappropriation of company or client assets - Violations of data protection laws or company security policies - Retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith

Disclosures are made to your manager and People Operations using the Conflict of Interest Declaration Form. Reporting Concerns Concerns about potential violations can be reported to: - Your manager or skip-level manager - People Operations (people@company.com) - The anonymous Ethics Hotline (details on the intranet) The company does not tolerate retaliation against employees who report concerns in good faith. Consequences Violations are investigated promptly and impartially. Outcomes depend on the severity of the violation and may include a formal warning, performance improvement plan, suspension, or termination.

Parental Leave Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Eligibility All employees who have completed at least six months of continuous employment are eligible for parental leave. This policy applies to birth parents, non-birth parents, and adoptive parents equally. Entitlement Role Duration Pay ------ ---------- ----- Primary caregiver 16 weeks 100% of base salary Secondary caregiver 4 weeks 100% of base salary Employees may extend leave beyond these periods using accrued annual leave, unpaid leave, or a combination. Extended leave must be agreed with People Operations at least four weeks before the planned start date. Notification Employees should notify their manager and People Operations as early as reasonably practicable, and no later than eight weeks before the intended leave start date. Written notice should include the expected start date and anticipated return date. Flexible Return Employees returning from primary caregiver leave may request a phased return of up to four weeks (e.g., 3 days/week for two weeks, then 4 days/week for two weeks before returning to full hours). Requests must be made at least two weeks before the planned return date and are subject to operational feasibility. Job Protection Employees on parental leave retain their role or an equivalent role at the same grade and compensation. Performance reviews during leave will not be penalised; employees will receive the average team rating for any review cycle occurring entirely during leave.

Benefits During Leave All benefits (health insurance, pension contributions, equity vesting) continue without interruption during paid parental leave. Keeping in Touch Employees on parental leave may, entirely voluntarily, work up to 10 "Keeping in Touch" days without affecting their leave entitlement. These days cannot be required by the company.

Learning & Development Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Philosophy We invest in employee growth because skilled, curious people build better products. Every employee is expected to spend time learning — not just when directed, but as an ongoing professional habit. Annual Learning Budget Each full-time employee receives an annual learning budget of $1,500 to spend on: - Online courses and learning platforms (Coursera, Pluralsight, O'Reilly, etc.) - Books and technical resources - Conferences and workshops (registration fee only; travel and accommodation are covered separately under the Expense Reimbursement Policy if the event is approved) - Professional certifications and exam fees Part-time employees receive a pro-rated budget based on contracted hours. The budget resets on January 1 each year and does not roll over. Approval Process Purchases under $200 can be made and expensed without prior approval. Purchases between $200 and $1,500 require manager approval via the HR portal. Requests above the annual budget cap require VP-level approval and a documented business case. Study Leave Employees sitting a professional certification exam are entitled to one paid study day per exam, up to a maximum of three study days per calendar year. Study days must be approved by the manager at least five business days in advance.

sitting a professional certification exam are entitled to one paid study day per exam, up to a maximum of three study days per calendar year. Study days must be approved by the manager at least five business days in advance. Internal Learning - A library of internal courses is available on the Learning Management System (LMS). - Employees are encouraged to share knowledge by running lunch-and-learn sessions. Facilitators receive a $50 voucher per session delivered. - Mentorship pairings are available through the HR portal. Both mentors and mentees are expected to commit to at least one hour per month for a minimum six-month engagement. Training Repayment If the company funds external training or a certification costing over $500 and the employee leaves within 12 months of completing it, a pro-rated repayment applies: - Departure within 6 months: 100% repayment - Departure between 6 and 12 months: 50% repayment - Departure after 12 months: no repayment Repayment does not apply if the employee is made redundant.

Anti-Harassment and Inclusion Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations & Legal Commitment The company maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards harassment, discrimination, and bullying. This applies to all employees, contractors, interns, and visitors in any work-related context — in the office, remote, at client sites, at company events, and on work-related social media. What Constitutes Harassment Harassment is unwanted conduct related to a protected characteristic (race, gender, gender identity, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, nationality, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law) that has the purpose or effect of: - Violating a person's dignity, or - Creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating, or offensive environment. Examples include (but are not limited to): offensive jokes, derogatory comments, unwanted physical contact, persistent unwanted personal attention, exclusion from work activities, and inappropriate messages. Sexual harassment includes unwanted sexual advances, requests for sexual favours, and any other verbal or physical conduct of a sexual nature. Reporting Anyone who experiences or witnesses harassment should report it through any of the following channels: 1. Direct report to manager — if the manager is not involved in the incident. 2. People Operations — people@company.com or in person. 3. Anonymous Ethics Hotline — details available on the intranet. Anonymous reports will be investigated to the extent possible given available information.

— if the manager is not involved in the incident. 2. People Operations — people@company.com or in person. 3. Anonymous Ethics Hotline — details available on the intranet. Anonymous reports will be investigated to the extent possible given available information. There is no time limit on reporting, but prompt reporting helps ensure a thorough investigation. Investigation Process All reports are taken seriously and investigated promptly, typically within 10 business days. Investigations are conducted by People Operations, with Legal involvement where appropriate. Both the complainant and the subject will have the opportunity to present their account. Confidentiality is maintained to the extent possible. Outcomes If harassment is substantiated, outcomes may include formal warning, mandatory training, transfer, demotion, or termination, depending on severity. Non-Retaliation Retaliation against anyone who makes a good-faith report or participates in an investigation is a separate, serious violation of this policy and will be dealt with as such. Training All employees complete anti-harassment training within their first 10 business days and annually thereafter. Managers receive additional bystander intervention and investigation training.

IT Acceptable Use and Security Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: IT & People Operations Scope This policy governs the use of all company-owned or company-managed devices, networks, software, and data — including systems accessed remotely. Acceptable Use Company technology resources are provided for business purposes. Incidental personal use is permitted provided it is brief, does not consume significant bandwidth, and does not involve any prohibited content or activities. Prohibited uses include: - Accessing, storing, or distributing illegal, obscene, or discriminatory content - Installing unlicensed or unauthorised software - Attempting to circumvent security controls or access systems without authorisation - Using company resources to operate a personal business or for extended personal activities - Sharing credentials with anyone, including colleagues Password and Authentication - All accounts must use passwords of at least 14 characters or passphrases. - Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all company accounts. - Passwords must not be reused across systems or shared via unencrypted channels. - A company-approved password manager is provided to all employees at no cost. Device Security - Company devices must have full-disk encryption enabled at all times. - Automatic screen lock must be set to 5 minutes or less. - Operating system and application updates must be applied within 72 hours of release. - Employees must not disable or circumvent endpoint protection software.

Data Handling - Customer data, employee data, and intellectual property are classified as Confidential and must be stored only in approved systems. - Confidential data must not be emailed to personal accounts or stored on personal devices or unapproved cloud services. - When in doubt about data classification, consult the Data Classification Guide on the intranet. Employees have no expectation of privacy on company devices or networks. Consequences Violations may result in suspension of access, disciplinary action, or termination.

Grievance Procedure Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Purpose This procedure provides a fair and consistent process for employees to raise workplace concerns. All grievances are handled with confidentiality and without fear of retaliation. What Is a Grievance? A grievance is a formal complaint about a workplace issue that has not been resolved informally. Examples include concerns about working conditions, application of company policies, interpersonal conflict, or perceived unfair treatment. Matters covered by the Anti-Harassment Policy follow a separate investigation procedure. Step 1 — Informal Resolution (Recommended First Step) Before raising a formal grievance, employees are encouraged to speak directly with the person involved or raise the matter with their manager. Many issues can be resolved quickly and informally. People Operations can provide coaching support at this stage on request. Step 2 — Formal Grievance If the informal approach fails or is not appropriate, the employee submits a written grievance to People Operations using the Grievance Submission Form (available on the intranet). The form should describe: - The nature of the grievance - Key dates and facts - Any individuals involved - The outcome the employee is seeking Acknowledgement: People Operations will acknowledge receipt within two business days.

Step 3 — Investigation A People Operations representative (or an appointed neutral investigator for complex cases) will: - Meet with the employee to understand the grievance in full - Interview relevant witnesses - Review any relevant documentation The investigation will be completed within 15 business days of acknowledgement, or the employee will be notified of a revised timeline. Step 4 — Outcome The employee will receive a written outcome within five business days of the investigation concluding. The outcome will explain the findings and any actions the company will take. Step 5 — Appeal If the employee is not satisfied with the outcome, they may appeal in writing to the Head of People Operations within 10 business days of receiving the outcome. The appeal will be reviewed by a senior leader who was not involved in the original investigation. The appeal outcome is final. Record Keeping Grievance records are kept confidentially in the employee's HR file and are retained for five years after the employee's departure.

Compensation and Pay Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations & Finance Pay Cycle Employees are paid on the last business day of each month via direct bank transfer. The payroll cut-off for changes (new hires, salary adjustments, terminations) is the 15th of each month. Changes received after the cut-off take effect in the following month's payroll. Salary Review Salary reviews are conducted once per year, following the annual performance review cycle (December). Adjustments, if any, are effective from February 1 of the following year. A salary review does not guarantee an increase. Factors considered in salary reviews include: - Annual performance rating - Position within the salary band for the role - Internal equity - External market benchmarking (conducted annually by People Operations) Salary Bands Every role is assigned to a salary band based on job level and function. Bands are reviewed annually against market data. Employees may request to know their band by contacting People Operations. The company does not disclose individual salaries. Bonus Programme Eligible employees (as defined in their employment contract) participate in an annual discretionary bonus programme. Target bonus amounts are expressed as a percentage of base salary by level. Actual payouts depend on company performance and individual performance ratings. Bonuses are paid in February, alongside the first payroll that reflects the salary review.

Offboarding Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Resignation Employees resigning from their position must submit written notice to their manager and People Operations. Notice periods by level: Level Notice Period ------- --------------- Individual contributor 2 weeks Senior / Lead 4 weeks Manager and above 6 weeks The company may, at its discretion, waive part or all of the notice period and pay in lieu. Notice Period During the notice period, the employee is expected to: - Continue performing their duties to the same standard - Participate in handover planning - Document ongoing work, processes, and contacts to a level agreed with their manager The company reserves the right to place an employee on garden leave during their notice period while continuing to pay their salary. Exit Interview People Operations will invite the departing employee to an exit interview, typically in the final week. Participation is voluntary. Feedback is aggregated and used to improve the employee experience; individual responses are kept confidential from the employee's manager. Equipment Return All company equipment (laptop, accessories, access cards, etc.) must be returned by the last day of employment. Employees will be invoiced for unreturned equipment at replacement cost. System Access IT will revoke all system access at end of business on the employee's last day, or earlier if required by security policy (e.g., involuntary termination). Employees should ensure personal files are removed from company systems before their last day; the company is not responsible for personal data left on company devices.

Final Pay The final pay run includes: - Salary up to and including the last day - Accrued but unused annual leave (paid out at the daily base rate) - Any approved outstanding expense claims submitted before departure Final pay is processed in the next regular payroll cycle following the last day. References People Operations provides standard employment verification references (dates of employment, job title) upon written request. Line managers may provide personal references in a personal capacity, clearly distinguished from official company references.

Health and Wellbeing Policy Effective date: January 1, 2024 Owner: People Operations Commitment The company is committed to supporting the physical, mental, and financial wellbeing of all employees. Wellbeing is not a perk — it is a business priority. Health Insurance All full-time employees and their immediate dependants are enrolled in the company health insurance plan from their first day of employment. Plan details, including coverage levels, in-network providers, and how to make a claim, are available in the HR portal under Benefits. Part-time employees working 20 or more hours per week are eligible for the individual (non-dependant) plan. Mental Health Support - Employee Assistance Programme (EAP): All employees have access to the EAP, which provides free, confidential counselling (up to 8 sessions per issue per year), legal advice, and financial coaching. The EAP is available 24/7 and can be accessed directly — no referral or manager involvement needed. - Mental Health Days: Employees may take up to 2 mental health days per year from their sick leave balance without providing a medical certificate. - Manager training: All people managers receive mental health first-aid training within six months of taking on a management role. Wellbeing Allowance Each employee receives a $600 annual wellbeing allowance to spend on activities or services that support their physical or mental health, including: - Gym memberships or fitness classes - Meditation or mindfulness apps - Ergonomic home office equipment (if not already provided under the Remote Work Policy) - Nutrition or sleep coaching

or services that support their physical or mental health, including: - Gym memberships or fitness classes - Meditation or mindfulness apps - Ergonomic home office equipment (if not already provided under the Remote Work Policy) - Nutrition or sleep coaching Claims are submitted via the HR portal with a receipt. The allowance is not transferable and does not roll over. Working Hours and Rest - Standard full-time hours are 40 hours per week. Consistent overwork is a management concern, not a badge of honour. - Employees are encouraged to take their full lunch break and to disconnect outside working hours. - Managers are expected to model healthy working habits and to address workload concerns raised by their team promptly. - Employees experiencing persistent workload issues should raise them with their manager, skip-level, or People Operations. Pregnancy and Fertility The company covers reasonable costs for fertility treatment not covered by the health insurance plan, up to $5,000 lifetime, through the EAP's specialist financial support service. Applications are made directly through the EAP and are completely confidential from the company. Review This policy is reviewed annually in January by People Operations in consultation with employee feedback collected during the prior year's engagement survey.

Password Reset Guide Category: Account Access Last updated: January 2024 Owner: IT Helpdesk Self-Service Reset (Recommended) If you have previously registered your phone number or recovery email with the identity provider, you can reset your own password without contacting IT. 1. Go to account.company.com/reset 2. Enter your company email address and click Send code 3. Enter the 6-digit code sent to your registered mobile number or recovery email 4. Choose a new password that meets the requirements below 5. Click Save — your new password is active immediately If the code does not arrive within two minutes, check your spam folder or click Resend. Codes expire after 10 minutes. Password Requirements - Minimum 14 characters - At least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, and one number - Cannot match any of your last 10 passwords - Must not contain your name or email address - Special characters are encouraged but not required Helpdesk-Assisted Reset If you cannot complete a self-service reset (e.g., you have lost access to your registered phone and recovery email): 1. Submit a ticket at helpdesk.company.com or call the IT Helpdesk at ext. 4357 (HELP) 2. You will be asked to verify your identity with your employee ID and manager's name 3. A temporary password will be issued via your personal email on file with HR 4. You must change the temporary password on first login — it expires after 24 hours

VPN Access Guide Category: Network Access Last updated: January 2024 Owner: IT Infrastructure What the VPN Is For The company VPN encrypts your internet traffic and routes it through the corporate network, giving you secure access to internal systems (code repositories, internal dashboards, on-premise databases) that are not reachable from the public internet. VPN use is mandatory when: - Accessing any internal system from outside the office - Working on any public or shared Wi-Fi network - Handling customer data or Confidential-classified company data remotely Getting Access VPN access is provisioned automatically for all employees on their first day. If you do not have the VPN client installed, submit a ticket at helpdesk.company.com with the subject "VPN client install request" and include your device model and operating system version. Installing the Client 1. Go to intranet.company.com/it/vpn 2. Download the installer for your OS (Windows, macOS, or Linux) 3. Run the installer — no admin password is required on company-managed devices 4. Sign in with your company email and password when prompted 5. Approve the MFA push notification on your registered device Connecting 1. Open the VPN client (look for the shield icon in your system tray or menu bar) 2. Select the Corporate – Standard profile 3. Phishing and Security Incident Reporting Category: Security Last updated: January 2024 Owner: IT Security Recognising a Phishing Attempt Phishing emails try to trick you into clicking a malicious link, downloading malware, or handing over credentials. Common warning signs: - Sender address does not match the claimed organisation (e.g., support@c0mpany.com) - Unexpected urgency ("Your account will be deleted in 24 hours") - Generic greetings ("Dear user") rather than your name - Links that show a different URL when hovered over - Attachments you were not expecting, especially .zip, .exe, or macro-enabled Office files - Requests for passwords, MFA codes, or financial transfers — legitimate internal teams will never ask for these by email What to Do If You Receive a Suspicious Email Do not click any links, download attachments, or reply to the sender. 1. Click the Report Phishing button in Gmail (the shield icon in the email toolbar) 2. Forward the email as an attachment to security@company.com 3. Delete the email from your inbox Reporting takes less than 30 seconds and helps IT block the threat for everyone. What to Do If You Clicked a Link or Entered Credentials Act immediately — speed matters: 1. Do not close the browser or shut down the computer 2. Disconnect from Wi-Fi (do not use the VPN disconnect — physically turn off Wi-Fi or unplug ethernet) 3. Call the IT Security line immediately: ext. 4358 (available 24/7 for incidents) 4. Do not attempt to fix it yourself — preserving evidence is critical

metadata.heading: What to Do If You Clicked a Link or Entered Credentials

text: (do not use the VPN disconnect — physically turn off Wi-Fi or unplug ethernet) 3. Call the IT Security line immediately: ext. 4358 (available 24/7 for incidents) 4. Do not attempt to fix it yourself — preserving evidence is critical IT Security will guide you through the next steps, which may include a password reset, MFA re-enrolment, and device scan. Other Security Incidents to Report Report any of the following immediately to security@company.com or ext. 4358: - Lost or stolen device (see also: Hardware Request Policy) - Suspected unauthorised access to your account (unexpected sign-in alerts, unknown sent emails) - Accidental sharing of confidential data to the wrong person or system - Ransomware or unusual file encryption on your machine - Suspicious USB devices found in the office Reporting Timeline Incident type Report within --------------- -------------- Phishing click / credential entry Immediately (call ext. 4358) Lost/stolen device 1 hour Accidental data disclosure 2 hours Suspicious email (no click) Same business day Under GDPR and applicable data protection laws, the company must report certain data breaches to the regulator within 72 hours of becoming aware. Employee delays in reporting are the most common reason this deadline is missed. Report first, investigate later.

Your account will be unlocked immediately Helpdesk Unlock If self-service is not available (e.g., you also do not have MFA access): 1. IT will unlock the account within 15 minutes during business hours Common Causes and Fixes Cause Fix ------- ----- Caps Lock was on Turn off Caps Lock and try again with your correct password Saved password in browser is outdated Clear the saved password, then type it manually Mobile device reconnecting with old password Update the password on your phone's mail/calendar app after a reset Shared machine still using old credentials Sign out of all sessions via account.company.com/sessions

Software Updates and Patching Policy Category: Security & Maintenance Last updated: January 2024 Owner: IT Security Why Updates Matter Software updates fix security vulnerabilities. Unpatched devices are one of the most common entry points for attackers. This is not optional maintenance — it is a security requirement. OS and System Updates Company laptops are managed via an MDM (Mobile Device Management) platform that pushes OS updates automatically. Timeline: - Critical security patches — deployed within 72 hours of release. A system notification will prompt you to restart. Do not postpone more than once. - Standard OS updates — deployed within 14 days. You will receive a notification with a scheduled maintenance window. - Major OS upgrades — tested by IT before rollout; deployed within 30 days of IT sign-off. You will receive at least one week's notice. If you dismiss a critical patch notification, IT will enforce the restart after 24 hours to protect the company network. Application Updates Managed Applications Applications distributed through the company's software management tool (Jamf for macOS, Intune for Windows) are updated automatically in the background. No action is required from you. Self-Installed Applications If you have installed approved software yourself (e.g., from the Software Catalogue): - Keep auto-update enabled where available - Check for updates manually at least once a week for high-risk tools (browsers, code editors, Docker) - Report outdated software you cannot update yourself to the IT Helpdesk

If you see a Relaunch to update prompt in the top-right corner of Chrome, relaunch the browser as soon as practical — do not leave it pending for more than 24 hours. Checking Your Patch Status You can check whether your device is compliant at compliance.company.com/my-device. A green status means your device is up to date. A red status means action is required — follow the instructions on the page or contact IT. IT runs a compliance report weekly. Devices that are non-compliant for more than five days will be contacted directly; devices non-compliant for more than 10 days may have network access restricted until patched. Requesting a Patch Deferral If an update is incompatible with a critical tool you need for work, submit a ticket with: - The update version and the affected application - Business justification for deferral - A proposed alternative timeline Deferrals are only granted for documented compatibility issues and are time-limited (maximum 30 days). Security patches cannot be deferred.
